_comment: Pinned local model roster for the on-prem NLP engine (NFR-2: nothing leaves the box).
Every id here was verified to exist and load on 2026-07-31. `make models` fetches them.
Hardware this was measured on: 12-core CPU, 15 GB RAM, NO GPU (Intel UHD only).

llm.role: Reasoning + structured extraction. Replaces the hosted Groq model.

measured.note: Thinking must be disabled (`think: false`). With thinking on, a single classification burned 500 tokens and 54 s without emitting an answer — NFR-1 allows 30 s total.

translation.role: Marathi <-> English. Used instead of the LLM because the LLM mistranslates legal Marathi (see notes).
translation.gate_note: Both repos are gated on HuggingFace. Accept the licence on each model page while signed in, then `hf auth login`. Ungated third-party mirrors exist (Raghavan/*, prajdabre/rotary-*) but are not the official weights and the rotary ones are a different architecture — do not substitute silently in a government deliverable.
translation.preprocessor: IndicTransToolkit (built from sdist on Python 3.14 — no cp314 wheel is published)

measured.note: CPU, num_beams=5, KV cache on (requires transformers 4.53.3). Verified correct on real GR Marathi: `सदर मान्यता ही कायम विनाअनुदानित तत्त्वावर राहील.` -> 'The approval will remain on a non-subsidised basis.'

embeddings.role: FR-4/FR-5 semantic clause search. Two separate indexes, per decision of 2026-07-31.

marathi.note: MahaSBERT-STS. Similarity-tuned; preferred over the NLI variant for retrieval.

english.note: English side of the two-index design. 768-dim, matching MahaSBERT so the two spaces are at least dimensionally comparable.

notes: Qwen3.5-2B mistranslated `सदर मान्यता` as 'the prevailing belief' (correct: 'the said approval'). This is the measured justification for routing all translation through IndicTrans2 rather than the LLM.

On a naive zero-shot prompt Qwen3.5-2B misclassified an explicit `रद्द करण्यात येत आहेत` ('are hereby cancelled') sentence as REFERENCES in Marathi and AMENDS in English. It fails in BOTH languages, so this is a prompt/scale limit, not a Marathi-specific weakness. It is NOT a fair comparison against the hosted model, which runs a tuned prompt in type_edges.py. Re-measure with the real prompt before drawing conclusions.
Groq settings are retained in .env for the planned local-vs-hosted agreement comparison. They are not a runtime dependency.
